arXiv:math/0408048v1 [math.AG] 03 Aug 2004

Two remarks on non-zero constant Jacobian polynomial map of  lC2\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-6.25958ptC}^{2}

revised version of that send to Ann. Pol. Math. by post at April 9, 2002
Nguyen Van Chau ††thanks: Supported in part by the National Basic Program on Natural Science, Vietnam. Affiliation: Hanoi Institute of Mathematics, P. O. Box 631, Boho 10000, Hanoi, Vietnam. Email: E-mail:nvchau@thevinh.ncst.ac.vn
Abstract

We present some estimations on geometry of the exceptional value sets of non-zero constant Jacobian polynomial maps of  lC2\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2} and it’s components.

2000 Mathematical Subject Classification: 14 H07, 14R15.

Key words and phrases: Exceptional value set, Jacobian conjecture.

1. Introduction. Recall that the exceptional value set EhE_{h} of a polynomial mapping h: lCm⟶ lCnh:\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{m}\longrightarrow\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{n} is the smallest subset Eh⊂ lCnE_{h}\subset\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{n} such that the restriction h:h−1​( lCn∖Eh)⟶ lCn∖Ehh:h^{-1}(\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{n}\setminus E_{h})\longrightarrow\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{n}\setminus E_{h} gives a locally trivial smooth fibration. The mysterious Jacobian conjecture (See [BMW] and [E]), which posed first by Keller in 1939 and still open even for two dimensional case, asserts that a polynomial map of  lCn\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{n} with non-zero constant Jacobian must be a polynomial bijection. Consider a polynomial map f=(P,Q): lC(x,y)2⟶ lC(u,v)2f=(P,Q):\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}_{(x,y)}\longrightarrow\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}_{(u,v)} and denote J⁡(P,Q):=Px​Qy−Py​QxJ(P,Q):=P_{x}Q_{y}-P_{y}Q_{x}. It is well-known that if J⁡(P,Q)≡c​o​n​s​t.≠0J(P,Q)\equiv const.\neq 0 but ff is not bijective, then the sets EPE_{P} and EQE_{Q} must be non empty finite sets and EfE_{f} is a curve so that each of it’s irreducible components is a polynomially parameterized curve ( the image of a polynomial map from lC into  lC2\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}) (See, for example in [J1, J2]).

In this note we present the followings.

Theorem 1. Suppose f=(P,Q)f=(P,Q) is a polynomial map with non-zero constant Jacobian. Then, a value u0∈EP\ u_{0}\in E_{P} if and only if the line u=u0\ u=u_{0} tangents to an irreducible local branch of EfE_{f}.

This theorem leads to the following fact that may be used to consider the non-existence of non-zero constant Jacobian polynomial maps with exceptional value curve of given types.

Theorem 2. The exceptional value set of a polynomial map of  lC2\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2} with non-zero constant Jacobian can not be isomorphic to a curve composed of the images of some polynomial maps of the form t↦(tk,q⁡(t))t\mapsto(t^{k},q(t)), k∈Nk\in\hbox{\rm\bf N}, q​(t)∈ lC​[t]q(t)\in\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}[t].

A special property of the curve with irreducible components given by parameterizations in theorem 2 is that it’s local irreducible branches may tangent to the only line u=0u=0. Simply connected curves are simple examples of such curves. This can be easy deduced from Lin-Zaidenberg’s theorem on simply connected curves (Theorem B in [ZL]).

Corollary 3. The exceptional value set of a polynomial map of  lC2\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2} with non-zero constant Jacobian can not be a simply connected curve.

Proofs of Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 will be presented in $ 3 and $4.

2. Preliminaries. In this section, we present some elementary facts which will be used in the proof of Theorem 1.

i) We will work with finite factional series with parameter ξ\xi of the form

(1) φ⁡(x,ξ)=∑k=1K−1ak​xnkm+ξ​xnKm,0≠ak∈ lC,nk∈Z,m∈N\varphi(x,\xi)=\sum_{k=1}^{K-1}a_{k}x^{n_{k}\over m}+\xi x^{n_{K}\over m},0\neq a_{k}\in\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC},n_{k}\in\hbox{\rm\bf Z},\ m\in\hbox{\rm\bf N}

with n1>n2>…>nKn_{1}>n_{2}>\dots>n_{K} and gcd⁡({nk:k≤K})=1\gcd(\{n_{k}:k\leq K\})=1.

Let h⁡(x,y)h(x,y) be a non-constant primitive polynomial monic in yy, degy⁡h=deg⁡h\deg_{y}h=\deg h. A fractional series φ⁡(x,ξ)\varphi(x,\xi) in (1) is called a Newton-Puiseux type of hh if

h⁡(x,φ⁡(x,ξ))=hφ​(ξ)+lower terms in ​x,hφ∈ lC​[ξ],deg⁡hφ>0.h(x,\varphi(x,\xi))=h_{\varphi}(\xi)+\mbox{lower terms in }x,\ h_{\varphi}\in\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}[\xi],\ \deg h_{\varphi}>0.

The Newton-Puiseux types of h⁡(x,y)h(x,y) can be constructed from Newton-Puiseux expansions at infinity of the curve h⁡(x,y)=0h(x,y)=0. In fact, if y=y⁡(x)y=y(x) is such a Newton-Puiseux expansion at infinity, then there is a unique Newton-Puiseux type φ\varphi of hh and a number ξ0∈ lC\xi_{0}\in\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC} such that y⁡(x)=φ⁡(x,ξ0)+ lower terms in ​xy(x)=\varphi(x,\xi_{0})+\mbox{ {\rm lower terms in }}x.

For a Newton-Puiseux type φ\varphi of hh the rational map Φ: lC× lC⟶ lC lP2\Phi:\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}\times\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}\longrightarrow\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-1.99168ptP}^{2} defined by

(2) Φ⁡(t,ξ):=(t−mult⁡(φ),φ⁡(t−mult⁡(φ),ξ)).\Phi(t,\xi):=(t^{-{\rm mult}(\varphi)},\varphi(t^{-{\rm mult}(\varphi)},\xi)).

determines a unbranched iφi_{\varphi} sheeted covering from  lC∗× lC\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{*}\times\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC} onto Φ⁡( lC∗× lC)⊂ lC2\Phi(\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{*}\times\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC})\subset\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}, where iφ:=mult(φ)/gcd{k:ak≠0,k<K}i_{\varphi}:={\rm mult}(\varphi)/\gcd\{k:a_{k}\neq 0,\ k<K\}. Hence, one can use the polynomial Hφ​(t,ξ):=h∘Φ⁡(t,ξ)H_{\varphi}(t,\xi):=h\circ\Phi(t,\xi) as a kind of “extension” of h⁡(x,y)h(x,y).

Lemma 4. ( See Theorem 2.4, [C]). Suppose h⁡(x,y)h(x,y) is a primitive polynomial and monic in yy. Then, c∈Ehc\in E_{h} if and only if cc is either a critical value of hh or a critical value of hφ​(ξ)h_{\varphi}(\xi) for any Newton-Puiseux type φ\varphi of hh.

In fact, by Newton’s theorem the polynomial h⁡(x,y)−ch(x,y)-c can be factorized as

ii) Consider a polynomial map f=(P,Q): lC2⟶ lC2f=(P,Q):\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}\longrightarrow\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}. By definition the exceptional value set EfE_{f} is composed by the critical value set of ff and the so-called non-proper value set AfA_{f} of ff - the set of all value a∈ lC2a\in\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2} such that there exists a sequence  lC2∋pi→∞\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}\ni\ p_{i}\rightarrow\infty with f⁡(pi)→a.f(p_{i})\rightarrow a. Following [J1], the non-proper value set AfA_{f}, if non-empty, is a curve composed by the images of some polynomial maps from lC into  lC2\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}.

f⁡(x,φ⁡(x,ξ))=fφ​(ξ)+lower terms in ​x,deg⁡fφ>0.f(x,\varphi(x,\xi))=f_{\varphi}(\xi)+{\mbox{\rm lower terms in }}x,\ \deg f_{\varphi}>0.

3. Proof of Theorem 1. We consider a polynomial map f: lC2⟶ lC2f:\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2}\longrightarrow\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}^{2} with non-zero constant Jacobian. Fix a suitable affine coordinate (x,y)(x,y) so that PP and QQ is monic in y.y. For a series φ\varphi in (1) represent

P⁡(x,φ⁡(x,ξ))=pφ​(ξ)​xaφmult⁡(φ)+lower terms in ​xQ⁡(x,φ⁡(x,ξ))=qφ​(ξ)​xbφmult⁡(φ)+lower terms in ​x,\begin{array}[]{c}P(x,\varphi(x,\xi))=p_{\varphi}(\xi)x^{\frac{a_{\varphi}}{{\rm mult}(\varphi)}}+\mbox{\rm lower terms in }x\\ Q(x,\varphi(x,\xi))=q_{\varphi}(\xi)x^{\frac{b_{\varphi}}{{\rm mult}(\varphi)}}+\mbox{\rm lower terms in }x,\end{array}

Now, assume the contrary that bφ<0b_{\varphi}<0. Then, there exists a Newton-Puiseux root at infinity u⁡(x)u(x) of the curve Q=0Q=0 such that u⁡(x)=φ⁡(x,ξ0)+lower term in ​xu(x)=\varphi(x,\xi_{0})+\mbox{lower term in }x. Proof of Theorem 1. If Ef=∅E_{f}=\emptyset, then ff is bijective and EP=EQ=∅E_{P}=E_{Q}=\emptyset. Hence, we need consider only the situation when Ef≠∅E_{f}\neq\emptyset. In this situation Ef=AfE_{f}=A_{f}, since ff has not singularity.

First, suppose the line u=u0u=u_{0} tangents to a local irreducible branch curve of an irreducible component ℓ\ell of AfA_{f}. By Lemma 5, there is a dicritical series φ\varphi of ff such that ℓ\ell is the image of fφ:=(pφ,qφ)f_{\varphi}:=(p_{\varphi},q_{\varphi}). By Lemma 6 (ii) the series φ\varphi is a Newton-Puiseux type both of PP and QQ. Since the line u=u0u=u_{0} tangents to ℓ\ell, u0u_{0} must be a critical value of pφp_{\varphi}. Hence, by Lemma 4 the number u0u_{0} is an exceptional value of PP.

Remark. From Lemma 6 (ii) and Lemma 5 one can easy see that the exceptional value set EfE_{f} of nonsingular polynomial map ff can not contains an irreducible component isomorphic to a line.

4. Proof of Theorem 2. Let f=(P,Q)f=(P,Q) be representation of ff in the coordinate in which EfE_{f} consists with the images of some polynomial maps of the form t↦(tk,q⁡(t))t\mapsto(t^{k},q(t)), k∈Nk\in\hbox{\rm\bf N}. By applying Theorem 1 we have that EP⊂{0}E_{P}\subset\{0\}. As ff has not singularity, PP is a nonsingular primitive polynomial. Then, from Suzuki’s equality

∑c∈ lC(χc−χ)=1−χ\sum_{c\in\hbox{\rm\ l\hskip-4.2679ptC}}(\chi_{c}-\chi)=1-\chi

(See in [S]) we get χ0=1\chi_{0}=1. Here, χc\chi_{c} and χ\chi indicate the Euler-Poincare characteristic of the fiber P=cP=c and the generic fiber of PP, respectively. Since the curve P=0P=0 is smooth, it has one connected component ℓ\ell diffeomorphic to lC. This component ℓ\ell must be isomorphic to lC by the Abhyankar-Moh Theorem [AM] and the restriction of ff on ℓ\ell must be injective. Then, as observed by Gwozdziewicz in [G], ff must be bijective. This is impossible, since Ef≠∅E_{f}\neq\emptyset.Q.E.D
